en: Using an inclined plane like a ramp reduces the force needed to lift heavy boxes, which helps prevent back injuries.
Wearing shoes with rubber soles increases friction with the ground, which prevents you from slipping on wet bathroom floors.
Because gravity pulls objects downward, stacking heavy books on the top shelf of a bookcase can cause it to tip over and injure someone.
Swallowing small neodymium magnets is extremely dangerous because they can attract each other inside the intestines and cause severe tissue damage.
Because water conducts electricity, you must never touch plugged-in appliances with wet hands to avoid receiving a dangerous electric shock.
Looking directly at the sun can permanently damage your retina, so you must wear special solar eclipse glasses to view it safely.
Listening to music through headphones at volumes above 85 decibels for extended periods can cause permanent damage to the hair cells in your ears.
Metals are excellent conductors of heat, which is why cooking pots have wooden or plastic handles to prevent your hands from getting burned.
Your body converts the chemical energy stored in food into mechanical energy for muscle movement and thermal energy to maintain a healthy body temperature.
Using a wheelbarrow, a type of lever, allows you to lift heavy garden soil with less effort, which saves your arm muscles from strain.
Touching a metal doorknob after walking on a carpet safely discharges built-up static electricity, preventing a sudden and painful spark shock to your finger.
Dark-colored clothes absorb more light and heat energy from the sun, so wearing white shirts keeps your body cooler during hot afternoons.
